label: Data types
gloss: a number and the text of a number are different things; arithmetic on text glues characters together instead of adding
why: Capture and copy-paste hand flows text that looks like numbers: "500", "$1,220.00". In JSON the quotes make it text, and text plus a number is string concatenation: "500" + 25 is "50025", and "$1,220.00" + 30 is not 1250. At Beacon, that turns a clean invoice into a quantity mismatch and a wrong variance. Fixing the types at the edge is cheaper than debugging every step after.
cue: when a total looks like digits mashed together, or a comparison that should be true is false, look at the quotes
task: The transform adds quantity + freeGoods and invoiceTotal + freight, and both come out wrong. Fix the record so the numbers are numbers: unitsBilled should be 525 (matching the PO) and variance should be 20.
notes: Numbers are bare: 500 not "500"; 1220 not "$1,220.00" (no quotes, no currency sign, no thousands comma).
Text stays quoted: "INV-1", "PO-1". true and false are bare words.
Run it after each fix and read the transform note in the trace.

checks.label: INV-1 variance is 20 (1220 + 30 freight - 1230 PO)
checks.why: only works once invoiceTotal is a number

checks.label: INV-1 qtyMatch is true (500 + 25 = 525 ordered)
checks.why: only works once quantity is a number
